hook.line: An 8×8 board and 20 counters a side. Enclose an enemy counter from both sides to take it: the game of the soldiers of ancient Rome.
hook.say: Ave! Let me show you the story of latrunculi.

ch.say: The Romans were mad about this game.
p: A strategy game whose name means the “game of soldiers (mercenaries)”, played all over the Roman Empire. The scholar Varro mentions it in the 1st century BC — the oldest record — and it appears in the poems of Ovid and Martial.
Its detailed rules have not survived: what is played today are reconstructions by researchers. Boards of several different sizes have been found in Roman Britain.

ch.cap: The 8×8 board: Black moves and encloses a white counter from both sides
p: Enclose an enemy counter between two of yours, in a row or a column, to capture it. In the standard game (Schädler’s) the enclosed counter is turned over, cannot move, and leaves the board at the start of your next turn.
Leave your opponent a single counter to win. If no counter can move, the side with more captures wins.
